mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over the last two months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when HOUST decreases by more than 10% over the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the last month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO increases by more than 2% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals strengthening consumer demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending drives economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when RSAFS increases by more than 1% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1%) signals accommodative monetary policy, which typically supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as low borrowing costs stimulate investment and economic activity.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% within the last month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased employment supports consumer spending and economic growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k & UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by less than 2% month-over-month, it signals strong economic growth without significant inflationary pressure, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real economic growth supports corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increase > 2% in 1 quarter & CPIAUCSL increase < 2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when both conditions are met.
